v.rationale: All three share nearly the same core: a #[Scope] inactiveFor with a grouped whereNull/orWhere, a command using the #[Signature]/#[Description] attributes (verified in the installed Laravel 13.40), filter_var validation, and Schedule::command()->dailyAt('06:00')->appendOutputTo(). All tests pass. Probes covered huge --days values, '+3' with whitespace, --days=0, future logins, and --days with no value; all three behave consistently, and none crashes. impl-3 ranks first: its log output is clear for the stated purpose ('so the number shows up in our logs'), its Pest.php edit is clean, its validation is tight, and its boundary tests are good. impl-2 is equally tight and adds a sensible index, but it prints a bare unlabeled number into an appended log file and leaves a commented-out line in Pest.php. impl-1 ranks last because it adds an unrequested Europe/Copenhagen timezone, which moves the run away from the 06:00 in the brief given the app is set to UTC. It also prints '1 users', uses the older $this->error() style, and leaves the same Pest.php comment, though its schedule test is the most thorough.
